content:
#1 According to oidification - table setoids are the oidification of pointed magmas with an endofunction. I am at a complete loss as to how this can be the case, especially compared to the other entries (e.g. groupoids (obviously), magmoids, r(i)ngoids, dagger categories, (differential) algebroids) which seem relatively straightforward.

  1. What does a “one object setoid” even mean? One isomorphism class?
  2. How could that concept be identified with that of a set equipped with the structure of a nullary, unary, and binary operator with no equational laws?

I apologize if this is something really simple but I am completely stumped with this entry.
subject: How are setoids the many-objectification of pointed magmas…

content: #2 Your confusion is understandable because, as mentioned on setoid, this same term is used to refer both to equivalence relations and pseudo-equivalence relations. You are assuming the definition as an equivalence relation, and yes there is a unique equivalence relation on a one-element set. But the table is using the definition as a pseudo-equivalence relation, which you could think of as “groupoid without any equations”. So then it makes sense that a one-object groupoid without equations gives you a group without equations.
